recs.abstract: This project will stabilize and document archeological collections from the Western Arctic Parklands to prevent deterioration and ensure long-term preservation. recs.abstract: At Joshua Tree National Park, a youth conservation crew of four to five members and one crew leader will complete six two-week field sessions to restore burned and damaged habitats. The crew will collect and plant native seeds, grow plants in a nursery, control invasive species, survey rare plants, and monitor vegetation health. recs.title: Process and Catalog Yellowstone Bison Management Records
recs.abstract: The focus of this project is to preserve, arrange, and catalog approximately 65 linear feet (LF) of the Yellowstone Archive’s backlog bison and ungulate management records. Cataloging these records will promote understanding of agency policies and activities, support research and public use, and ensure their long-term preservation.

The project equips youth with practical skills while helping parks maintain reliable information for staff and visitors.
recs.impact: Without funding, the parks will lack updated maps and accurate resource data, limiting staff’s ability to make informed decisions and respond quickly during emergencies such as fires or search-and-rescue events.

recs.title: Zion Cultural Resources
recs.abstract: This project supports the protection and management of cultural resources in Zion National Park by identifying and evaluating heritage sites, conducting historic research, and applying standard cultural field methods. It provides management recommendations, documents historic structures, and develops preservation strategies. The work concludes with concise summary reports that guide long-term stewardship. The projects involve resources in visible, high visitation areas with beneficiaries including visitors, participating members of the project, and park staff.
recs.impact: If this project is not completed, significant cultural sites in Zion National Park may remain unidentified, undocumented, or at risk of damage. Gaps in research, preservation planning, and management guidance would hinder informed decision-making, potentially resulting in permanent loss of cultural heritage and reduced protection for historic structures.

recs.title: Zion National Park Resource Management Archivist
recs.abstract: This project is a multi-year project for an archivist to work for approximately sixty-six weeks to complete archive projects in collaboration with National Park Service museum and archives professionals. The archivist will be engaged in the processing of an estimated 60 linear feet of Zion National Park resource management archives and create and publish a finding aid on the park website accessible to researchers and the public. The archivist will also perform monthly tasks associated with integrated pest management, and environmental monitoring, accessioning, updating or generating loan documentation, working with incoming research permits, answering research requests, conducting annual inventories, and assisting the museum curator with a variety of duties as they arise.

recs.title: Museum and Archives Collaboration
recs.abstract: This project encompasses a review of all Zion National Park museum accession records prior to 1995 and appropriate actions to resolve discrepancies. A temporary museum technician will review all pre-1995 accession files, perform a 100% inventory of all relevant collections, resolve data discrepancies, and prepare deaccession documents for long-missing items and items outside the scope of collection for internal review by the Collection Advisory Committee.
recs.impact: If this project is not awarded, addressing inaccurate collection information will not be possible, leading to unreliable data for determining the needs of the collections, decreased efficiency, and increased time wasted on piecemeal solutions to these problems.
